atoms.b: Many young people struggle to find a balance between ((individual)) freedom and the expectations of ((society)).
Their ((identity)) often depends on a sense of ((belonging)) to a group, but also on the pursuit of ((self-realisation self_realisation)) — becoming who they truly are.
At the same time, ((self-preservation self_preservation)) can make people cautious: they might avoid risks that threaten their ((esteem_needs)), like the desire for ((prestige)) or recognition.

Yet life is often ((ambiguous)): success in one area can feel like failure in another. For example, true ((accomplishment achievement)) may come not from fame, but from ((volunteer_work voluntary_work)), where helping others leads to personal growth.
In the end, individualism and social responsibility are not ((mutually_exclusive)) — they can coexist.
